definitions.explanation: Used when something turns out as anticipated.
Used when returning to an original conclusion.

examples.japanese: やはり{雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}った。
やはり{難|むずか}しかった。
やはり{彼|かれ}が{犯人|はんにん}だった。
examples.english: As I thought, he was the culprit.

examples.japanese: {調|しら}べてみたら、やはり{予想|よそう}{通|どお}りだった。
examples.english: When I looked into it, it was just as I predicted.

examples.japanese: {何度|なんど}も{練習|れんしゅう}したが、やはり{本番|ほんばん}では{緊張|きんちょう}した。
examples.english: I practiced many times, but as expected I was nervous during the real performance.

examples.notes: やっぱり is casual form

examples.english: I'm going to quit after all.

examples.japanese: やはりこれが{一番|いちばん}いいと{思|おも}う。
examples.english: I think this is the best after all.

examples.japanese: {考|かんが}え{直|なお}して、やはり{買|か}うことにした。
examples.english: After reconsidering, I decided to buy it after all.

examples.japanese: いろいろ{迷|まよ}ったが、やはり{最初|さいしょ}に{見|み}つけた{店|みせ}に{戻|もど}ることにした。
examples.english: I wavered back and forth, but in the end I decided to go back to the first shop I found.

examples.japanese: やはり{日本|にほん}が{好|す}きだ。
やはり{母|はは}の{料理|りょうり}が{一番|いちばん}だ。
examples.english: My mother's cooking is still the best.

examples.japanese: {何度|なんど}{見|み}ても、やはり{美|うつく}しい。
examples.english: No matter how many times I see it, it's still beautiful.

examples.japanese: {長|なが}い{間|あいだ}{離|はな}れていたが、やはり{故郷|ふるさと}はいいものだ。
examples.english: I was away for a long time, but my hometown is still a wonderful place.

examples.japanese: {何年|なんねん}{経|た}っても、やはりあの{映画|えいが}が{一番|いちばん}{心|こころ}に{残|のこ}っていると{思|おも}う。
examples.english: Even after many years, I still think that movie is the one that left the deepest impression on me.

notes:
やはり expresses that something matches expectations or remains unchanged.

FORMS:
- やはり: standard
- やっぱり: casual, colloquial
- やっぱ: very casual

USAGE:
- Often at the beginning of a sentence
- Expresses confirmation of expectations
- Can show a return to original opinion
